title: National Parks Traveler Relives History in Southeastern US
titleZh: 国家公园旅行者：在美国东南部重温历史
credits: Julie Taboh reported on this story for VOANews.com. George Grow adapted this story for Learning English. Ashley Thompson was the editor.

sentences.en: American Mikah Meyer has an unusual goal.
sentences.zh: 美国男子米卡·迈耶有一个不寻常的目标。

sentences.en: He wants to visit all of the more than 400 properties operated by the National Park Service.
sentences.zh: 他想要参观国家公园管理局运营的全部400多处保护地。

sentences.en: He spent January 2017 visiting historic areas in the southeastern United States.
sentences.zh: 2017年1月，他走访了美国东南部的历史遗迹。

sentences.en: One of his first stops was Fort Sumter, a former military position in waters just off the coast of Charleston, South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 他最初到访的地方之一是萨姆特堡，这是位于南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿海岸附近水域的一处废弃军事据点。

sentences.en: Fort Sumter is famous for being the place where the first shot of the Civil War was fired.
sentences.zh: 萨姆特堡之所以闻名，是因为美国内战的第一枪就是在这里打响的。

sentences.en: It is also where the first person killed in the conflict died.
sentences.zh: 这里也是这场冲突中第一位遇难者长眠之地。

sentences.en: After years of rising tensions between Northern and Southern states, the two sides clashed in Charleston Harbor on April 12, 1861.
sentences.zh: 在南北各州紧张关系持续升级多年之后，双方于1861年4月12日在查尔斯顿港发生冲突。

sentences.en: That was when the Southern army launched an artillery attack on Fort Sumter.
sentences.zh: 正是在那时，南方军队对萨姆特堡发动了炮击。

sentences.en: Federal troops surrendered the fort a short time later.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，联邦军队就投降了这座堡垒。

sentences.en: Union forces eventually fought to regain control of the base, and defeated the South in 1865.
sentences.zh: 联邦军队最终经过奋战重新夺回了基地的控制权，并于1865年击败了南方。

sentences.en: As he stood inside the large walls of Fort Sumter National Monument, Mikah Meyer looked across the water to the port at Charleston.
sentences.zh: 当米卡·迈耶站在萨姆特堡国家纪念区的高大城墙内时，他望向水面，看到了查尔斯顿的港口。

sentences.en: He imagined what the area must have looked like more than a century and half ago.
sentences.zh: 他想象着这一带在一个半世纪前的样子。

sentences.en: “You’ll see across that bridge, Charleston, South Carolina.
sentences.zh: “隔着那座桥，你就能看到查尔斯顿，南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: It was under siege at one point for 17 months.
sentences.zh: 这里一度被围困了17个月。

sentences.en: There were cannons that could fire from where I’m standing on the fort all the way to the old town…”
sentences.zh: 从我此刻所站的堡上，一直到老城，都部署着能够开炮的大炮……”

sentences.en: Meyer also visited the Charles Pinckney National Historic Site in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 迈耶还参观了南卡罗来纳州的查尔斯·平克尼国家历史遗迹。

sentences.en: There he had a chance to learn about Charles Pinckney, who helped write – and was a signer of -- the U.S. Constitution.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他有机会了解查尔斯·平克尼，他参与起草了美国宪法，并是宪法的签署人之一。

sentences.en: “Some people call him our forgotten founding father, but he was a political figure of early America who helped shape what our eventual constitution ended up looking like…”
sentences.zh: “有些人称他为被我们遗忘的建国先贤，但他确实是早期美国的一位政治人物，对后来我们宪法的最终面貌产生了重要影响……”

sentences.en: The National Park Service helps care for what remains of Pinckney’s former home and farm.
sentences.zh: 国家公园管理局帮助守护着平克尼故居和农场仅存的部分。

sentences.en: Park service workers tell the stories of 18th- century plantation life for free and enslaved people.
sentences.zh: 公园管理局的工作人员免费讲述18世纪种植园中自由人和被奴役者的故事。

sentences.en: During his travels in January, Meyer had a surprise.
sentences.zh: 在1月的旅行中，迈耶遇到了一件意外之事。

sentences.en: Barack Obama, in his last few days as president, named a new national park site in Beaufort, just south of Charleston.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马在卸任总统前的最后几天，在查尔斯堡以南的博福特宣布设立一处新的国家公园遗址。

sentences.en: It is called the Reconstruction Era National Monument.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“重建时期国家纪念地”。

sentences.en: The Reconstruction Era stretched from 1861 to 1898.
sentences.zh: “重建时期”从1861年延续至1898年。

sentences.en: It was a period when Americans struggled with the treatment of newly freed African Americans.
sentences.zh: 那是一个美国人不断反思如何对待新获非裔美国人的时期。

sentences.en: The new national monument will help tell that story.
sentences.zh: 这座新的国家纪念地将有助于讲述这段历史。

sentences.en: “So all within the Charleston, South Carolina, area you have these three sites now that are really related to either America becoming America, or America figuring out who America is…”
sentences.zh: “因此，在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯堡地区，你现在可以看到这三个彼此关联的遗址，它们都与‘美国如何成为美国’或‘美国如何认清自我’息息相关……”

sentences.en: Driving south into the state of Georgia, Meyer stopped at Fort Pulaski National Monument.
sentences.zh: 向南驶入佐治亚州时，迈耶在普拉斯基堡国家纪念地停了下来。

sentences.en: Many observers believe the creation of Fort Pulaski was a major turning point in U.S. military history.
sentences.zh: 许多观察者认为，普拉斯基堡的建成是美国军事史上的一个重要转折点。

sentences.en: Built in 1861, the former base is considered one of the most modern posts of its time.
sentences.zh: 这座建于1861年的旧军营被视为当时最先进的军营之一。

sentences.en: It had a moat, with water that surrounded the whole fort.
sentences.zh: 它外围环绕着护城河，河水将整个堡垒团团围住。

sentences.en: Just an hour’s drive south, Meyer visited Fort Frederica on St. Simons Island.
sentences.zh: 再往南驱车一小时，迈耶参观了圣西蒙斯岛上的弗雷德里克堡。

sentences.en: He walked among the ruins of this former 18th-century settlement.
sentences.zh: 他漫步在这座18世纪旧聚落的废墟之间。

sentences.en: Continuing south, he visited the Timucuan Ecological and Historic Preserve in Jacksonville, Florida.
sentences.zh: 继续南下，他参观了位于佛罗里达州杰克逊维尔的提穆夸生态与历史保护区。

sentences.en: He learned that a plentiful supply of oysters provided food for the Native Americans who once lived there.
sentences.zh: 他了解到，丰富的牡蛎为曾经生活于此的印第安人提供了食物。

sentences.en: Meyer noted that some areas are covered with oyster shells.
sentences.zh: 迈耶指出，部分地区被牡蛎壳所覆盖。

sentences.en: Former wetlands are now walkable because the remains of shells have turned into earth.
sentences.zh: 昔日的湿地如今已可步行通行，因为这些贝壳的残骸已化作泥土。

sentences.en: Meyer explains how oyster shells are used as building materials.
sentences.zh: 迈耶解释了牡蛎壳如何被用作建筑材料。

sentences.en: “And it’s all of these little huts that were built out of a kind of paste of oyster shells and other minerals that, when mixed together, form, you know, sort of a brick-like substance…”
sentences.zh: “这些都是用牡蛎壳与其他矿物混合而成的糊状物筑成的小屋，混合之后，你会看到，形成了一种类似砖块的物质……”

sentences.en: Continuing down the Florida coast, Meyer stopped at Castillo de San Marcos National Monument in the city of Saint Augustine.
sentences.zh: 继续南下佛罗里达海岸，迈耶在圣奥古斯丁市停在了圣马科斯堡国家纪念地。

sentences.en: He also stopped at another former military post, the much smaller Fort Mantanzas.
sentences.zh: 他还参观了另一处前军事据点——规模小得多的曼坦扎斯堡。

sentences.en: Meyer said visiting these historic places helped him recognize the many things the National Park Service does to protect national treasures for all to enjoy.
sentences.zh: 迈耶说，参观这些历史遗迹帮助他认识到国家公园管理局为保护国家瑰宝、让全民共享所做出的诸多努力。

sentences.en: I’m Caty Weaver.
sentences.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

sentences.en: And I’m Ashley Thompson.
sentences.zh: 我是阿什利·汤普森。
